title: One step of the W process
statement: For natural numbers $n,k$, a function $a\colon\mathbb{N}\to\mathbb{N}$, and a state $(b,v)$ consisting of a Boolean list and a natural-number list, define the next state as follows: if $b$ is done, keep $(b,v)$ unchanged; otherwise, if $b$ is acceptable at length $|v|$, replace it by its remainder and append the value determined by $n,k,a,v,b$ to $v$; if neither condition holds, return the empty Boolean list together with $v$.
hypotheses_covered: A function from natural numbers to natural numbers
A state consisting of a Boolean list and a natural-number list
caveat: The meanings of the done and acceptable predicates, remainder operation, and value operation are not included in the supplied definitions.
